claims.text: Greg Short asserts that allowing a significant business loss to make you psychologically skittish is the primary failure mode after a setback; the correct response is to immediately pivot to identifying the next opportunity rather than dwelling on the loss.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Applies to business operators who have just taken a significant inventory or financial loss
claims.mechanism: Dwelling on a loss consumes time and attention that should be redirected toward solving the resulting constraint; psychological skittishness prevents the decisive action required to recover.

claims.text: Greg Short describes moving from absorbing a major loss on a Wednesday to actively sourcing placement for 150,000 units by the following Thursday, illustrating that a 24-hour pivot from loss to opportunity-seeking is operationally feasible and strategically necessary.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Consumer packaged goods context with a summer SKU launch deadline within 10 days of the loss event

numbers.axis: time elapsed from loss event to pivot action

anchors.event: major loss on summer SKU absorbed
active sourcing of placement for 150,000 cases begun

examples.text: Greg Short recounts that the week before a summer SKU launch (10 days out), he took a major loss on that product. On Wednesday the loss happened; by Thursday he had already shifted focus entirely to finding where to place the 150,000 cases rather than dwelling on the setback. He frames this as the only acceptable response: you cannot let losses turn you into a skittish operator.

practices.text: After absorbing a significant business loss, immediately redirect attention to the next available opportunity rather than processing the loss emotionally.
